newsitem.title: USA: Int'l FiberCom sees $32 mln 1997 revs.
newsitem.headline: Int'l FiberCom sees $32 mln 1997 revs.

text.p: International FiberCom Inc said on Wednesday it has raised its 1997 revenue forecast to over $32 million.

"Our backlog has increased to $14 million, and we have now raised our forecast for 1997 revenues to over $32 million, an increase of approximately 200 percent over 1996," Joseph Kealy, president, said in a statement.
The company also said its unit, Kleven Construction Inc, has been awarded a contract for fiber-optic upgrade projects from Cox Communications Inc.

The contract is a result of Cox Communications' expansion and upgrading of its cable television network and system in Phoenix with fiber-optic cable. The company said the contract, with upgrades, should generate about $8 million in revenue in 1997. Cox has told International FiberCom that it should expect revenues from the Phoenix system upgrade through the year 2000, the company said.

The company also said it is close to closing the acquisition of all the outstanding stock of a privately held telecommunications service located in the southeast U.S. The acquisition candidate has annual revenues of $14 million and has recorded 13 consecutive years of profitability.
International FiberCom designs, installs and maintains fiber-optic and other cable services.
